title: Pitch campaigns: one email per brand, sent slowly from your Gmail

features.title: Pitch campaigns
features.body: Pick a saved list of brand contacts and a template, and the app writes one pitch to each brand, to its best-ranked person, never two people at the same brand. Templates fill in their first name, the brand, why you fit and your media kit and rate card from My links, so they use no Claude at all (Personalise adds one opening line per brand with Claude, at half price). Every pitch waits in Drafts until you press Approve. Approved emails go out a few minutes apart, on weekdays during the brand's working hours: 10 a day the first week, growing to at most 30 (you can choose up to 50). A reply from anyone at a brand stops that brand's emails. If nobody answers after the follow-ups, the app tries the next person once.

features.title: Pitches that follow the rules
features.body: Every campaign email ends with your name, your business postal address and a line saying they can reply "no thanks". Anyone who does, or whose address bounces, is never emailed again. Sending pauses by itself after 2 bounces or 1 "no thanks" in a day, until you press Resume. Add your postal address (a PO box works) in Settings, Deals & money, Pitch campaigns before your first campaign.

title: Find more people at a brand, and check emails before you send

features.title: Find more people at this brand
features.body: Open any deal and press Find more people: the app asks Hunter.io who works at that brand and adds them to People at this brand, ranked, with partnerships and PR people first. It uses no Claude. Hunter's free plan gives 50 credits a month (one per brand you look up), and the app never goes past that unless you raise the limit. Add your free Hunter key in Settings, Accounts, Contact finders, where you also see how many credits are left. An Apollo key can be added too, as a second finder.

features.title: Emails are checked before you send
features.body: Press Check address on anyone to make sure the address exists (half a Hunter credit). Every night the app also checks for free that each brand can receive email at all. Addresses that don't exist are marked, drop to the bottom, and can never be pitched, so fewer emails bounce and your Gmail stays healthy. People who have replied to you count as checked. Addresses at brands that accept everything can't be proven, so automatic follow-ups skip them and wait for you to press Send.

title: Everyone at every brand, best person first

features.title: Brand contacts
features.body: A brand can now have lots of people saved, not just one email. Brand contacts (under More, or in the sidebar on a laptop) lists everyone the app found in your brand emails, with job titles and phone numbers from their signatures. Each person gets a score: people who have replied to you rank highest, especially the ones who led to deals and answer fast, then partnerships and PR inboxes. New pitches go to the top person at the brand. Open any deal to see everyone at that brand and add someone.

features.title: No duplicates, and a do-not-email list
features.body: The same email is never saved twice, and brands that share a website are flagged so you can merge them in one tap. Press Don't email on anyone and no pitch or follow-up can go to them again; if someone replies asking you to stop, that happens by itself. Forget deletes everything about a person. You can also import a spreadsheet (including Hunter or Apollo exports) and download everything as a CSV.

title: A Day summary that fits your screen

features.title: Day summary in two columns on a laptop
features.body: On a laptop, Day summary now puts what still needs you first: Still waiting on you, then Lined up for tomorrow, in the wide column. New deals today and What you got done sit beside them on the right, so you no longer scroll past a long list to find them. Tomorrow shows the first four things (press Show more for the rest), and long notes show two lines; the full note is on Today and on the deal. Your phone looks exactly the same as before.

title: A laptop layout with room to breathe

features.title: A sidebar, and pages that use your whole screen
features.body: On a laptop or big screen, every page now has its own place in a sidebar on the left: Today, Drafts, Deals and Money at the top, then Day summary, My links, Settings, Help and What's new, so nothing hides under More any more. Deals, Pitching brands, Money and Drafts now stretch to fill a wide screen. Your pitches show one tidy line each, with the five follow-ups as a row of dots (green once sent, orange for the next one); hover over the dots to see the dates. Your phone looks exactly the same as before.

title: Colours that tell you where each deal is

features.title: Every stage has its own colour
features.body: On Deals, each stage now has its own colour and icon: blue for new and waiting, amber while you're talking it through, violet while you're making the content, green once it's posted, and teal while you wait to be paid. The coloured row above your deals is the filter: press a stage to see only those deals, and All to see everything again.

features.title: A tidier Today
features.body: Do these first now stands out at the top. Every other section has a coloured icon and shows how many things are in it, so you can see at a glance where the work is. Drafts shows the first three, with See all to open the rest, and New opportunities folds its list until you press Show all.

title: Check before it goes, undo after

features.title: A last look, and ten seconds to undo
features.body: When you press Send on a draft, you now see exactly what the brand will get first: who it's to, the subject, the message and any PDF attached. Press Keep editing to go back, or Send to send it. After that, a bar at the bottom counts down ten seconds with an Undo button, so a message sent by mistake never leaves. Follow-ups you've set to go out automatically still send on their own, as before.

features.title: One set of simple icons
features.body: The little pictures next to headings, deal stages and your day summary are now simple line icons that look the same on your laptop and your phone, instead of emoji that changed from one device to another. Deal stages read plainly too: New lead, Negotiating, Contract to sign, Posted, Payment pending.

features.title: Try anything without touching your real deals
features.body: Open More and press Start practice. A copy of the app opens with made-up brands like Bloomleaf Tea and Juniper Juice, so you can answer emails, send invoices, ask Claude for drafts and move deals along to see what happens. An orange bar at the top says you're practising. Nothing there is real: Send only pretends, and your own deals, emails and accounts are never in it. Press Leave practice to go back. Each time you start, the sample brands begin fresh.

features.title: Everything working? in one place
features.body: The top of More now shows one card that answers it: Claude, Gmail, Instagram, backups and updates, each with a tick or a short sentence in plain words, like "Connected, last checked 9:30 AM" or "Stopped connecting on Tuesday". Anything that needs you gets one button that fixes it: Reconnect, Back up now, Update now. Today shows the same thing on one line, only when something needs a look. Google asks you to sign in again every 7 days while your Google app is in testing, so this is where you'll see it first.

title: An app icon on your phone and laptop

features.title: Add Creator CRM to your phone's home screen
features.body: Open Creator CRM on your phone, then add it to your home screen. On Android, open the browser menu (the three dots) and press Add to Home screen or Install app. On iPhone, press the Share button in Safari, then Add to Home Screen. The orange Creator CRM icon appears next to your other apps, and it opens full screen, without the browser's address bar.

features.title: Its own window on your laptop
features.body: On your laptop, Creator CRM now opens in a window of its own, with no tabs or address bar, and its own button on the taskbar. It uses Microsoft Edge behind the scenes, so if it asks you to sign in once, use the same username and password as always.

title: Clearer messages when something goes wrong

features.title: Problems explained in plain words
features.body: When Gmail, Instagram, Claude or a backup runs into trouble, the app now says what happened and what to do, such as "Gmail needs you to sign in again. Press Reconnect Gmail." or "Couldn't reach Instagram. Check this computer is online." The technical details are still there under Details if someone helping you needs them. The status line at the top also says "Checking for new messages" and "Claude is reading 3 messages" instead of computer words.

title: A clearer bar at the bottom of your phone

features.title: Bigger, clearer buttons along the bottom
features.body: On your phone the five buttons at the bottom are bigger and easier to read, and the place you're in now sits in a soft orange pill, so you always know where you are. The grey box that used to stay stuck on the last button you tapped is gone, the bar keeps clear of the iPhone's home line, and the top of the screen has the app's logo and a rounder search box. Today's greeting is a little smaller so your list starts higher up.

features.title: A setup guide that holds your hand
features.body: Setting up on a new computer is now one step per screen: your name, Claude, Gmail, then your rates. Each step says why the app needs it and exactly what to click, with links straight to the right page and a Copy button for the address Google asks for. It opens by itself until Claude and Gmail are connected, and you can open it again any time from More or Settings.

features.title: Settings in five tabs
features.body: Settings used to be one very long page. It now has tabs: Accounts for your connections, You for your name, voice, rates and to-do rules, Deals & money for follow-ups, invoices and contracts, App for updates, nightly backups and Claude spending, and Advanced for the things you rarely need, like Claude models, extra Instagram options and restoring a backup.

features.title: One draft at a time
features.body: Drafts now works like your email inbox. A short list on the left shows each brand, what kind of message it is, its first line, and a yellow tag if it still has a blank to fill in. Press one to open it beside the list. On your phone, the list fills the screen; press a draft to read it, and All drafts to go back. When you write a draft from a deal, an invoice or Today, it opens straight away.

features.title: Pictures, links and layout in every email
features.body: Brand emails in a deal now show the way they did in Gmail: their pictures, colours and buttons, with every link clickable. Long emails are folded until you tap Show the whole email, and earlier messages in the thread sit behind Show earlier messages. Emails are cleaned before they're shown, so nothing in them can run inside the app.

features.title: A tidier Pitching brands page on your phone
features.body: Finding brands to pitch now fits your phone screen: the search box gets its own line, the search depth choice stays inside the card with its price showing first, and the Draft pitch, Edit contact and Dismiss buttons line up under each brand. No more grey strip down the side.

features.title: Five places instead of nine
features.body: The top bar now has just Today, Drafts, Deals, Money and More. Deals holds your deals and the brands you're pitching; More has your day summary, links, Settings and Help. Today starts with the three things to do first, and the rest of the day's list is folded underneath, one tap away. On your phone the five places sit at the bottom of the screen, where your thumb is.

features.title: No more blanks sent to brands
features.body: When your rates or a link aren't in Settings yet, Claude leaves a blank like [RATE FOR 1 REEL] for you to fill in. Drafts now point these out in yellow, and the app won't send an email or DM, or an automatic follow-up, until every blank is filled in. And if Gmail or Instagram stops connecting, a red bar on every page tells you, with a button to reconnect.

features.title: A step-by-step view of each deal
features.body: Once a brand says yes, the deal shows its steps: contract, product (for gifted deals), creating the content, the brand's approval, posting, the invoice and payment. The step it's at now is highlighted with its due date and what to do next. Claude reads every email you get or send and moves the deal to the right step by itself, even when a few steps happen at once. If something happened outside email, one button moves it on.

features.title: Show brands how their post did
features.body: When a deal is marked Posted, the app finds your post on Instagram, or you paste its link. A week later it reads the post's reach, views, likes, comments, saves and shares, and drafts a thank-you email to the brand with a one-page results PDF attached and an idea for working together again. You check it in Drafts before anything is sent. For TikToks or Stories, type the numbers in on the deal.

features.title: Know what a to-do is about without opening the email
features.body: When a brand email gives you something to do, the to-do now has a short summary from Claude: what they're asking, what the opportunity is, the pay or perks, and what you need ready. For an application form it says what the form asks for and what it's for. Links from the email (forms, briefs, contracts) sit right on the to-do. Read email opens the deal at that email in one click, and Open in Gmail jumps to the original. You can add your own rules for how Claude writes to-dos in Settings, About you.

title: Deal dates on your Google Calendar

features.title: Your deal dates, on your phone
features.body: Contracts to sign, content due, posting days and payments now go on a calendar called Creator CRM in your Google account. Dates move when a deal changes and disappear when they're done. To turn it on, press Reconnect Gmail in Settings once and allow calendar access. A deal also warns you when its dates clash with another brand's exclusivity, so you can check the two don't compete.

features.title: Spot the catches before you sign
features.body: When a brand emails a contract as a PDF, Claude reads it and the deal shows a checklist: when you get paid, the fee, how long they can use your content in ads, exclusivity, revision rounds and a kill fee. Anything outside your limits is marked red or amber, and a Review contract task appears on Today. For contracts on DocuSign and similar sites, paste the text on the deal to check it. Set your limits in Settings, Contract check.

features.title: Your day at a glance
features.body: Day summary has a fresh look. At the top you see how many things you got done, what's still to do, new deals and what's lined up for tomorrow; press any of them to jump there. Each thing you did today shows the brand and the time. Things still waiting have Done and Open buttons right there, and if drafts are ready to send there's a button to review them.

title: Ask Claude to change a draft

features.title: Ask Claude to change a draft
features.body: Under every draft there's now an Ask Claude to change it box. Press Warmer, Shorter, More formal or Add my rates, or type what you want, like 'mention I'm free in March'. Claude rewrites the draft in your voice and keeps the facts and numbers. Nothing is sent: it waits for you to read it and press Send. Undo puts back the version from before. Each change costs about 3 cents of Claude credit.

features.title: Know what to ask for
features.body: Open a deal you're still deciding on and a What to ask for box shows a price for what the brand wants, line by line: each Reel, Story, TikTok or post, plus extra for paid usage and exclusivity. Your prices come from your last paid deals, or from the rates in About you until you have five. It also says how far under your rate their offer is. Change the number if you like and press Draft counter, and a friendly counter-offer quoting exactly that amount waits in Drafts for you.

features.title: See brands already engaging with you
features.body: Outreach now lists accounts that tagged you in a post, @mentioned you or commented on your recent posts, so you can pitch brands that already know you. Press Add as lead and it joins your brand leads, ready for Draft pitch, or press Not a brand to hide it. To allow this, press Reconnect Instagram once on the Settings page.

features.title: Look up any brand on Instagram
features.body: Connect Facebook on the Settings page (your Instagram needs to be linked to a Facebook Page) and Outreach can look up a brand's Instagram by handle: followers, bio, an email in the bio and the creators it tags in sponsored posts. Brands found with Find brands get these details too, pitches use them, and fans are hidden from the accounts engaging with you. Nothing is scraped; it all uses Instagram's official API.

features.title: See which leads are worth your time
features.body: Every new lead now shows High value, Medium or Low value on Today and in Pipeline. The score comes from what the brand offered: paid or gifted, the budget compared with your usual deal, whether a budget was mentioned, and whether they've paid you before. Hover over it to see why. Nothing extra is sent to Claude.

features.title: Say no to several leads at once
features.body: In Pipeline, pick Low-value leads, tick the ones that aren't a fit and press Decline selected. A short, polite no-thanks is written for each. In Drafts, read them and press Approve all declines to send them together. Each deal closes as declined.

features.title: Find anything in seconds
features.body: A search box at the top finds any brand, contact, old email or DM, or invoice, and opens it with one click. Press / to jump to it. Pipeline, Outreach, Money and Drafts each have their own search and filters, and you can click a column name to sort by it. Click a status count on Pipeline, or a total on Money, to see just those. Your filters stay as you left them. Inside a deal you can search the conversation. And after an update, the app now reloads the tab you already have open instead of opening a new one.

features.title: Bring your Linktree over in one click
features.body: The Links page has a fresh look: each link is a card with its own colour, and your Instagram, TikTok and YouTube sit at the top as quick buttons. Under Add links, choose From Linktree, paste your Linktree link and press Find links. You see everything it found, untick anything you don't want, rename if you like, and press Add. Links you already have are skipped, and tracking bits like ?utm_source are left off. You can also paste a list of links, one per line. Drafts use these exact links whenever a brand asks for your portfolio or shop.

features.title: Work with past brands again
features.body: Brands that paid you before are the easiest yes. Each week the app writes a few short re-pitches to brands that paid you and have gone quiet for two months, and to brands whose gifted collab went up a couple of weeks ago, suggesting a paid one this time. Each re-pitch mentions your last collab, shows on Today under Rebook past brands and waits in Drafts for you. Sending one adds a new pitch with follow-ups. You can also press Pitch them again on any finished deal. Change the quiet period and how many a week under Settings, Rebooking past brands.

features.title: Late payments get a polite nudge
features.body: When an invoice is 3, 7 and 14 days past its due date, a short reminder with the invoice attached is written for you, a little firmer each time. Today shows which brands are late, and every reminder waits in Drafts for you to check and send, even if follow-ups go out automatically. Reminders stop the moment you mark the invoice paid. Change the days, or turn reminders off, under Settings, Invoices.

features.title: Your data is backed up every night
features.body: Creator CRM now saves an encrypted backup of all your deals, messages and settings every night and keeps the last two weeks. When you have OneDrive, the backups go into it, so a copy is safe even if the laptop is lost or breaks. If the laptop is off at night, it backs up soon after you open the app. To turn it on, go to Settings, Automatic backups and choose a passphrase once. Write the passphrase down, because without it a backup can't be opened.

features.title: Always running, even after a restart
features.body: Creator CRM now opens quietly in the tray when you sign in to your laptop, so new emails and follow-up reminders keep coming in, and the app keeps working from your phone, even after the laptop restarts for an update. Nothing pops up; click the tray icon or the desktop shortcut when you want it. You can turn this off under Settings, Start with Windows.

features.title: See what Claude costs, and get warned before credits run out
features.body: Settings now shows how much has been spent on Claude in total, this month, and on reading messages, writing drafts and finding brands. Type in your credit balance from the Claude Console and a yellow banner appears when about 20% is left. If the credits run out, a red banner says so, the app stops trying until you top up, and the developer is told automatically.

features.title: Claude costs less
features.body: Reading your messages now uses Claude Sonnet, which costs about half as much and still sorts deals well. Drafts still use the best model. Find brands has a Search depth choice: Quick, Standard or Thorough, each showing roughly what one search costs. Big email imports are analyzed at half price in the background, so older deals fill in over a few hours. In Settings you can switch either model, with the rough cost next to each option.

features.title: Send an invoice in two clicks
features.body: When a brand asks for your invoice, open the deal and press Create invoice. The amount and what you made are filled in from the deal, and numbers run INV-2026-001, 002 and so on. Email invoice puts a short note with the PDF attached in Drafts, so you check it before it goes. Add your address and how brands pay you once, under Settings, Invoices.

features.title: See what you've earned and what's late
features.body: The new Money tab shows what's booked, what's invoiced and waiting, what came in this month and what's overdue. Overdue invoices also show on Today. When the money lands, press Mark paid; the app never decides that for you. Export CSV gives you the year's invoices for taxes.

features.title: Something not working? Tell us in one click
features.body: Under Help, describe what went wrong and press Report a problem. Your note and the app's recent activity go to the developer so it can be fixed in the next update. When the app runs into an error by itself, it sends a short report automatically. Email addresses, phone numbers, passwords and keys are removed first. You can turn automatic reports off in Settings.

features.title: Find brands to pitch
features.body: On the Outreach page, describe the kind of brands you want to work with. Claude searches the web for brands that fit you, finds the partnerships email each brand publishes (with the page it came from) and suggests a pitch idea. Draft pitch puts a personal pitch in Drafts for you to edit and send. Nothing is sent without your click.

features.title: Your Instagram numbers in every draft
features.body: Once Instagram is connected, Settings shows your followers, engagement rate and 28-day reach, refreshed every day. Drafts quote these exact numbers when brands ask for your stats.

features.title: Updates install themselves
features.body: When a new version is out, a banner at the top says what's in it. Click Update now: Creator CRM backs up your data, installs the new version and opens again by itself. Nothing installs without your click.

features.title: What's New and Help videos
features.body: After every update this page shows what changed, with a short video for each new feature. You can rewatch all of them any time under Help.

features.title: Your links in one place
features.body: The new Links tab holds your Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, website and portfolio. Drafts use these exact links instead of placeholders.

features.title: Pick when follow-ups are drafted
features.body: Under Settings, Follow-ups, choose the daily time follow-ups are prepared. You can also turn on sending email follow-ups automatically at that time; everything else still waits for your approval.

features.title: Drafts learn how you write
features.body: Every message you send is kept next to Claude's original draft. New drafts borrow from your closest past messages, especially ones you edited and ones brands answered. You can see the examples, leave any out, or switch this off in Settings.
